short_bio: Actor and producer who won consecutive Best Actor Oscars for Philadelphia and Forrest Gump.
biography:
Tom Hanks grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area and went from the sitcom Bosom Buddies (1980–1982) to film comedy with Splash in 1984. Big, in 1988, earned him the first of his Academy Award nominations.

In 1994 he won the Best Actor Oscar for Philadelphia and a year later won again for Forrest Gump, making him the second performer after Spencer Tracy to take the award in consecutive years. He also voiced Woody in Toy Story (1995) and starred in Saving Private Ryan (1998) and Cast Away (2000).

With Gary Goetzman he co-founded the production company Playtone in 1998; its credits include the HBO miniseries Band of Brothers and The Pacific. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016.
